confirmed.title: POST /api/pierre/email/send persists status="sent" and returns deliveryAccepted:true without ever calling ANY email provider
confirmed.currentBehavior: The route's only imports are `next/server` and `@supabase/supabase-js` (lines 1-2); grep for resend|sendEmail|EmailProvider|communications in the file returns 0. It fabricates a provider message id (l.389-391), INSERTs into `pierre_outbound_emails` with `status: "sent"` + that fake id (l.412-413), writes a `pierre_task_logs` entry `event: "email_sent_direct"` / `Email envoyé : <subject>` (l.448-449), and answers HTTP 200 with `deliveryAccepted: true` (l.506). No email is ever transmitted. This is NOT a dev-only stub: it is an authenticated App Router route and `src/hooks/pierre/usePierreMissionCenter.ts:1090` (`sendDirectEmail`) POSTs to it from the Pierre Mission Center UI, then merges the returned `status:"sent"` record into `directEmails` state so the UI displays it as sent. The launch-readiness registry (src/lib/launch-readiness/route-readiness.ts:40) lists ONLY `/api/pierre/email/draft` with the note "draft only — no live send" — this /send route is not registered at all, so the go-live inventory believes no live send surface exists.
confirmed.failureScenario: An authenticated user in the Pierre Mission Center sends an HR email to an employee (e.g. a document delivery or an end-of-probation notice). The API returns 200 {ok:true, provider:{deliveryAccepted:true}}. The DB row in pierre_outbound_emails reads status='sent' with provider_message_id='pierre_1751...'; the mission timeline reads 'Email envoyé : Fin de période d'essai'. The employee never receives anything. The company later relies on that row + mission log as proof it notified the employee on that date — the evidence is entirely fabricated, and there is no failed/unknown state anywhere to reveal it.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Either (a) route this handler through the governed pipeline (pierre/v1 communications intents/deliveries, or sendEmailProduction) and set status from a real provider acknowledgement, or (b) if it must stay a stub, make it fail-closed: persist status='not_sent'/'blocked_no_provider', drop provider_message_id, drop deliveryAccepted:true, do not log 'Email envoyé', and return a non-success payload. A record must never reach status 'sent' without a provider ack.
confirmed.regressionTest: POST /api/pierre/email/send as an authed user with no email provider configured; assert the response does NOT contain deliveryAccepted:true, the inserted pierre_outbound_emails row status is NOT 'sent', and no pierre_task_logs event claims 'Email envoyé'.

confirmed.title: Client-supplied `field_values` overwrite the authoritative DB values printed in the contract (name, employer, salary, effective dates)
confirmed.quotedCode:
const extra: Record<string, string | null> = { "employment.start_date": dateStr(version.effective_from), "employment.end_date": dateStr(version.effective_to), ...fieldValues };
    const requested = Array.from(new Set([...policy.required_fields, ...policy.conditional_fields, ...Object.keys(fieldValues)]));
confirmed.currentBehavior: `fieldValues` is the raw HTTP body map from POST /api/pierre/v1/contracts/[id]/generate (`field_values: b.field_values ?? {}` → `apiGenerateContract` → `generateContract`, no filtering anywhere). It is (a) spread LAST into `extra`, so it overrides even the contract version's own persisted `effective_from`/`effective_to`, and (b) unioned into `requested`, so any canonical path the caller names is loaded. `buildStrictGenerationContext` then does `if (input.extra_values && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(input.extra_values, path)) values[path] = input.extra_values[path];` (generation-context.ts:113) — the caller value WINS over the value actually loaded from the DB. The only validation is `resolveFieldPolicy(path)` (path must be canonical); the VALUE is never validated (no type/format check except weekly_hours) and never compared to the employee/contract record. `required_provenance: "payroll_system"` on `compensation.base_salary` (field-policies.ts:43) is enforced nowhere in production — `evaluateFieldUsage` has no non-test caller.
confirmed.failureScenario: HR user with document.write POSTs to /api/pierre/v1/contracts/<id>/generate with body {"field_values":{"employment.weekly_hours":"35","employee.last_name":"DUPONT","company.legal_name":"ACME LUX SARL","employment.start_date":"2020-01-01","compensation.base_salary":"120000"}} while the DB says last_name=MARTIN, company name=Acme France, version.effective_from=2026-03-01 and no payroll record exists. Readiness returns ready (all required fields are 'present'), the PDF/DOCX are rendered from the forged values, canonical_hash is computed over them, the contract is approved → finalized → ready_for_signature. The signed employment contract now states a different employee, a different employer, a start date 6 years earlier and a salary that never came from payroll, all contradicting the HR record the rest of the system uses (activation, amendment effects).
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Do not merge caller-supplied values into the generation context. Either drop `field_values` entirely and resolve every canonical path server-side from the DB, or restrict `extra_values` to a hard allowlist that the contract layer itself computes (start/end date from the version row only, never from the body) and require any remaining caller path to (a) be absent from the canonical loader and (b) satisfy its `required_provenance` via `evaluateFieldUsage`. `extra` must spread `fieldValues` FIRST so the version's persisted dates always win.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: create a CDI contract for employee MARTIN (effective_from 2026-03-01), then call generateContract with field_values {"employee.last_name":"DUPONT","employment.start_date":"2020-01-01"} and assert it either throws or that the rendered model/canonical hash still contains MARTIN and 2026-03-01.

confirmed.title: Ambiguous/garbled decide_validation defaults to APPROVE — the human HR approval gate is satisfied by an unsafe default
confirmed.currentBehavior: The server derives the canonical payload for a decide_validation tool call. Any decision string it does not recognise — including the empty string produced by `String(a.decision ?? "")` when the model omits the argument, or a French phrasing like "attends", "ne valide pas", "non" (no "rejet"/"chang" substring) — falls through to `return "approve"`. The persisted proposal payload becomes `{ decision: "approve", ... }` and /api/assistant/execute then calls the real V1 approve endpoint (decideValidationV1 → POST /api/pierre/v1/validations/{id}/approve), which in mission-service.decideValidationAction transitions the gated task ready → queued and enqueues it for the worker.
confirmed.failureScenario: User: « Fais le nécessaire pour Paul. » with a pending validation on a sanction/contract draft. The model emits tool_call {name:"decide_validation", arguments:{}} (no decision, no id). proposal-builder computes decision = normalizeDecision("") = "approve", persists it, and returns label "Approuver cette validation". The user clicks the single confirm button; the server records validation_approved with actor_id = the user and unblocks the task Pierre was NOT allowed to run without human review. A decided validation is final (decideValidationAction returns early when v.status !== "pending"), so it cannot be undone.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Make the decision explicit-or-nothing: return null (no proposal) unless the model's decision string maps unambiguously to approve/reject/request_changes. `approve` must never be a fallback value for an unrecognised or missing argument.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit test on buildAndPersistProposal: toolCall {name:'decide_validation', arguments:{}} and {arguments:{decision:'je ne sais pas'}} must both return null (no persisted proposal); only {decision:'approve'} may produce a payload with decision === 'approve'.

confirmed.title: A hallucinated/absent validation_id silently retargets the FIRST pending validation, and the confirm label never names the target
confirmed.currentBehavior: resolvePendingValidationV1 is called by proposal-builder with `String(a.validation_id ?? "")`. If the model invents a UUID that does not exist, or omits the argument, byHint is null and the code falls back to the first pending validation found while iterating the company's 25 most recent missions. proposal-builder then builds the label from the decision only — `label = decision === "reject" ? "Rejeter cette validation" : ... : "Approuver cette validation"` (proposal-builder.ts:94) — and useCloneChat.ts:326 renders exactly `prop.label` as the confirm button. The human confirms an approval of a validation that is never identified anywhere in the response (no mission title, no task, no reason).
confirmed.failureScenario: Company has two pending validations: V1 = « courrier disciplinaire — Paul » and V2 = « avenant salaire — Sarah ». User: « Fais le nécessaire pour Paul. » The model calls decide_validation with validation_id "val_paul" (invented). byHint = null → the server picks V2 (first pending in list order) and shows « Approuver cette validation ». The user clicks, believing it concerns Paul; Sarah's salary amendment is approved and queued instead. Nothing in the UI or the payload ever named V2.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Never fall back to a positional pick: if the model's validation_id does not resolve to a real pending validation, return null (no executable proposal) and ask the human which validation. When a proposal IS built, the label/preview must carry the resolved target identity (mission title + validation reason), as governed-turn.ts:109 does with its {type:'validation'} block.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: 2 pending validations; buildAndPersistProposal with arguments {validation_id:'does-not-exist', decision:'approve'} must return null (today it returns a proposal targeting the first pending one). Second assertion: any decide_validation proposal returned must include the resolved mission/validation identity in its label or preview payload.

confirmed.title: Employee auto-resolution by partial name: first match wins, substring matches both directions, no ambiguity check
confirmed.currentBehavior: findPierreEmployeeByName (and detectEmployeeReferenceFromText, employee.ts:343-361, which scans the free-text instruction and `return e` on the first employee whose full name — or all of whose name tokens — appear) are called from the live mission front door src/app/api/pierre/use/submit/route.ts:1001 and :1011. Both return the FIRST match in registry order and never check whether a second employee also matches. The reverse containment `needle.includes(e.full_name)` means a name the registry does not contain resolves to a different, shorter-named employee. The resolved employee is then used to load their real 360 file snapshot (submit/route.ts:1025), is injected into the LLM brain context (runPierreFinalBrain employeeContext) and into task payloads via enrichPayloadWithEmployeeContext.
confirmed.failureScenario: Registry contains « Paul Martin » (id A) and « Paul Martineau » (id B). Instruction « Fais le nécessaire pour Paul Martineau » → findPierreEmployeeByName returns « Paul Martin » (listed first, and "paul martineau".includes("paul martin") is true) with no warning. The mission, the generated HR documents and the sensitive 360 snapshot fed to the model are all bound to the WRONG employee, while employeeResolutionSource is reported as a confident 'explicit_name'/'text_detection'.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Collect ALL matches instead of `find`; if more than one non-archived candidate matches, return an ambiguity result and make Pierre ask « Lequel : Paul Martin (site X) ou Paul Martineau (site Y) ? ». The deterministic gate already exists — src/lib/pierre/v1/cognitive-runtime/entity-resolution.ts resolveEntity returns status 'ambiguous' with distinguishers — but it is wired to nothing except a p16a self-check (ultimate/p16a/command-center.ts:134). Also drop the reverse `needle.includes(full_name)` containment.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit test on findPierreEmployeeByName/detectEmployeeReferenceFromText with two employees sharing a first name (and one whose full name is a substring of the query): the function must NOT return a single profile, and the submit route must refuse to bind employee_context and surface a disambiguation question instead.

confirmed.title: Human-approval gate can be discharged on the WRONG validation: the server silently retargets `decide_validation` to the first pending validation it finds, and the confirm UI never names the target
confirmed.currentBehavior: `byHint` is computed INSIDE the per-mission loop, so it can only win on the first mission that has any pending validation. If the user's validation lives on mission #3 while mission #1 has any pending validation, the loop returns mission #1's validation and the hint is discarded entirely. The same happens when the model omits/hallucinates `validation_id` (the live chat route calls `buildAndPersistProposal` directly and never runs `validateToolArgs`, so `String(a.validation_id ?? "")` can legitimately be ""). proposal-builder.ts:90-94 then persists the proposal with a generic label (`"Approuver cette validation"`) and the client (useCloneChat.ts:325-328) renders it with `payload: {}` — the human confirms an approval whose target is never displayed. /api/assistant/execute then calls `decideValidationV1` on that substituted id. Worse, the validation CARD shown in the thread is resolved independently client-side (governed-turn.ts:106 `ctx.validations.find(x => x.id === vid) ?? ctx.validations.find(x => x.status === "pending")`), so the item displayed and the item approved can be two different rows.
confirmed.failureScenario: Company has mission A = "Envoie le contrat" (guard red ⇒ task awaiting_validation, HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED) created first, and mission B = expense-report review created later. User types "approuve la validation de la note de frais". Model emits tool_call decide_validation{validation_id: "<B's id>", decision: "approve"}. resolvePendingValidationV1 iterates missions, reaches A first, `byHint` is null for A's list, `vals.find(pending)` returns A's CONTRACT validation → proposal persisted for A. UI shows only "Approuver cette validation". User clicks Confirmer → /api/assistant/execute → decideValidationV1 approves the CONTRACT gate the user never intended to approve; the contract task leaves awaiting_validation and resumes. The single human-approval floor protecting sensitive HR actions is discharged by consent given for a different object.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Never substitute a target for an effectful action. `resolvePendingValidationV1` must (a) search the hinted id across ALL missions before any fallback, and (b) return null when a hint was supplied and did not resolve — no "first pending" fallback for approve/reject. When no hint is supplied at all, refuse the proposal and ask the user which validation (or route to the cockpit). Additionally, the persisted proposal must carry a target-identifying label (mission + reason + validation id/short ref) and the client must render it, so a confirmation can never be blind. Same fix for the client-side preview in governed-turn.ts:106.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit-test resolvePendingValidationV1 with two missions where mission[0] has a pending validation and mission[1] holds the hinted id: assert it returns the HINTED validation (or null), never mission[0]'s. Route test: POST /api/assistant/chat with a model tool_call carrying an unknown validation_id ⇒ assert no proposal is persisted (or proposal is refused), and assert the persisted proposal's label contains the target reference.

confirmed.title: Server proposal path never runs validateToolArgs / isToolAvailable — the tool-arg governance is dead code on the authoritative path
confirmed.quotedCode: proposal = await buildAndPersistProposal({ toolCall: structured.tool_call ?? null, userMessage: message, identity: ctx, conversationId, proposals: stores.proposals, req, at: now() });
confirmed.currentBehavior: The raw, unvalidated `structured.tool_call` from the model goes straight into buildAndPersistProposal, which persists an executable proposal. The governance functions that DO validate — isToolAllowedInMode / isToolAvailable / validateToolArgs — only exist inside assembleFromStructured (governed-turn.ts:209-219), whose sole consumer is the CLIENT hook src/app/assistant/useCloneChat.ts:317. Worse, useCloneChat.ts:322 explicitly discards that governed output (`.filter((b) => !(b.type === "action_preview" && b.action.requiresConfirmation))`) and then renders the Confirm button purely from the server proposal with `allowed: true` hardcoded (line 327). So TOOL_REGISTRY's `decide_validation: { args: ["validation_id", "decision"] }` requirement — which the existing test openai-layer.test.ts:71 asserts — is never enforced on the path that actually executes.
confirmed.failureScenario: Model emits tool_call {name:"decide_validation", arguments:{}} — no validation_id, no decision. validateToolArgs would return {ok:false, missing:["validation_id","decision"]} and block it, but it is never called server-side. buildAndPersistProposal instead does String(a.validation_id ?? "") = "" and String(a.decision ?? "") = "", which resolvePendingValidationV1 turns into the first pending validation and normalizeDecision turns into "approve". A completely empty tool call from the model becomes a persisted, one-click "Approuver cette validation" on the termination dossier.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Call isKnownTool + isToolAllowedInMode(mode) + isToolAvailable + validateToolArgs on the server, inside/before buildAndPersistProposal, and return null (no proposal) when any check fails. The client-side assembleFromStructured must not be the only place governance runs — it is decorative, since useCloneChat.ts:322 throws its action away.
confirmed.regressionTest: Route test for /api/assistant/chat: stub the responder to return tool_call {name:"decide_validation", arguments:{}} and assert the JSON response has `proposal === null`. Repeat for each effectful tool with missing/blank required args.

confirmed.title: resolvePendingValidationV1 / resolveCancellableMissionV1 silently retarget to an arbitrary pending validation or active mission when the model's id hint does not resolve
confirmed.currentBehavior: When the model supplies a hallucinated or empty validation_id (likely — the model has no real UUIDs unless it first called list_validations), byHint is null and the code falls back to the FIRST pending validation found across the company's 25 most recent missions. The same pattern exists at line 111-112 for cancel: `const pick = byHint ?? active[0] ?? null;` picks an arbitrary active mission. The human-facing label built from this (proposal-builder.ts:94) is just "Approuver cette validation" — it names no employee, no mission, no subject, so the confirming human cannot see which decision they are approving (contrast cancel_mission, which does render the mission title).
confirmed.failureScenario: Model calls decide_validation with validation_id "val-abc123" (hallucinated) and decision "reject". No such id exists ⇒ byHint is null ⇒ the fallback selects the first pending validation, which is the HUMAN_ONLY termination validation of an unrelated employee. The proposal targets that validation. The user sees an unlabelled "Rejeter cette validation"/"Approuver cette validation" button and confirms, believing it applies to what they were discussing. A binding HR decision is recorded against the wrong employee's dismissal file.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Never fall back to an arbitrary target for an effectful decision. If the hint does not resolve to exactly one real pending validation (or active mission), return null so no proposal is built, and have the model ask the user to pick one. Additionally, the proposal label for decide_validation MUST name the concrete subject (mission summary / employee) so the human's confirmation is informed consent.
confirmed.regressionTest: Test resolvePendingValidationV1 with hintId="does-not-exist" against a company that has a pending validation: assert it returns null (not the first pending). Test with hintId="": assert null. Same for resolveCancellableMissionV1. Add a proposal-builder test asserting the decide_validation label contains the mission/employee subject.

confirmed.title: Communication delivery idempotency_key is derived from a freshly-generated random recipient UUID → concurrent intent creation sends the SAME email twice
confirmed.quotedCode:
const recipientId = newUuid();                                     // line 109
...
const idem = sha256(Buffer.from(`${ctx.company_id}:${intentId}:${recipientId}:${channel}`));   // line 123
...
 values ($1,...,$18,now()) on conflict (company_id, idempotency_key) do nothing`,             // line 141
...
`select id, kind, payload from pierre_rt_outbox where company_id=$1 and status='pending' and comm_processing_status is null order by created_at asc limit $2`  // line 65-66 (no FOR UPDATE / SKIP LOCKED)
confirmed.currentBehavior: createCommunicationIntents() claims nothing: it SELECTs pending outbox rows with no row lock (l.65), dedups the INTENT on (company_id, dedup_fingerprint) (l.157) and dedups the DELIVERY on (company_id, idempotency_key) (l.141, backed by uq_pierre_rt_comm_delivery_idem). But that delivery key is sha256(company:intentId:recipientId:channel) where recipientId = newUuid() (l.109) — a fresh random value on every pass. pierre_rt_communication_recipients has no semantic unique index (only uq_...recipient_company_id on (company_id,id), which a fresh uuid always satisfies), so the recipient insert at l.110-113 has no ON CONFLICT and always succeeds. The sequential replay case is saved only because the `existing` intent lookup at l.91 short-circuits before l.109 — it does NOT survive concurrency.
confirmed.failureScenario: Two runtime workers each claim a runtime job for the SAME company (queue.ts claimJobs default tenant_concurrency_cap = 1000000, so per-company parallelism is unbounded). Both run runtime-action-handlers.ts:146 `createCommunicationIntents(tx, ctx.tenant, ...)`, which scans ALL pending outbox rows of that company. T1 and T2 both read pending outbox row R (no lock). Both find no intent for source_event_key (l.91). T1 inserts intent I; T2's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING blocks on the unique index, then re-selects and gets the SAME intentId I (l.160). T2 then inserts recipient r2 (≠ r1) at l.109-113, computes idem = sha256(co:I:r2:'email') ≠ sha256(co:I:r1:'email'), so the delivery INSERT does NOT conflict → TWO 'queued' email deliveries for the same intent/recipient/channel. dispatchCommunicationDeliveries then claims each delivery independently and sends each with its own frozen provider_idempotency_key (`communication:<co>:<delivery_id>:<hash>`, l.136/278), which contains the delivery id — so even Resend's idempotency header cannot collapse them. Result: the employee receives the SAME governed email twice (e.g. a contract signature link, a validation request, a disciplinary notice). Same race via /api/pierre/v1/communications/dispatch (cron) overlapping with runtime-scheduler.ts:178.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: The delivery fingerprint must bind the DETERMINISTIC recipient identity, never a random uuid. Two changes: (1) build idem from the resolved identity — sha256(`${company}:${intentId}:${recipient_type}:${resolved_user_id ?? resolved_email}:${channel}`) — so a second pass over the same intent produces the SAME key and the existing unique index uq_pierre_rt_comm_delivery_idem collapses it; (2) add a unique index on pierre_rt_communication_recipients (company_id, intent_id, recipient_type, coalesce(resolved_user_id::text, resolved_email,'_')) and make the insert at l.110 `on conflict ... do nothing` + re-select the id. Additionally, claim the outbox row at l.65 with `for update skip locked` so two dispatchers never process the same event concurrently.
confirmed.regressionTest: On the real-PG harness: seed one pending pierre_rt_outbox row with a communicable kind + a resolvable recipient, then run TWO createCommunicationIntents() transactions CONCURRENTLY (start both, commit both). Assert `select count(*) from pierre_rt_communication_deliveries where company_id=$1 and intent_id=$2 and channel='email'` = 1 and `select count(*) from pierre_rt_communication_recipients where intent_id=$2` = 1. Today both are 2, and the FakeEmailProvider records 2 sendEmail calls with two different idempotencyKeys.

confirmed.title: Cockpit mission idempotency key is `ui|<companyId>|<instruction>` with no actor, no nonce and no time window → re-submitting the same instruction is a PERMANENT silent no-op reported as success
confirmed.currentBehavior: The cockpit calls client.createMission({instruction, source}) with no idempotency_key (api-client.ts:120), so the key is the raw instruction text scoped to the company only. pierre_rt_missions carries `unique (company_id, idempotency_key)` (supabase/migrations/2026-06-15__pierre_v1_runtime.sql:73) and MissionRepo.byIdempotency (repositories.ts:72-76) matches it FOREVER — there is no TTL, no day bucket, no per-submission nonce, and the key does not even include the actor. A second submission of the same text returns the first mission with idempotent_replay: true and HTTP 200. `idempotent_replay` is declared in the Zod schema (client.ts:37) and set (mission-service.ts:102/218) but is read by NO UI code — grep finds it only in tests.
confirmed.failureScenario: An HR manager submits "Fais le point sur les absences de la semaine" in the cockpit composer on Monday → mission M1 is created and completes. The following Monday the same text is submitted again → POST /api/pierre/v1/missions carries idempotency_key `ui|<companyId>|Fais le point sur les absences de la semaine` → byIdempotency returns the already-`done` M1 → the API answers 200 with M1 and idempotent_replay: true → submitPierreMission returns { ok: true } → MissionComposer clears the field and shows success. Pierre NEVER receives the new mission and no task is ever queued. Recurring HR instructions (monthly payroll prep, weekly absence review, annual-review reminders) are exactly the shape that breaks. A second user in the same company typing the identical text is likewise handed the first user's mission.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: The idempotency key must identify ONE SUBMISSION ATTEMPT, not the instruction text for all time. Have the composer generate a nonce per submit (crypto.randomUUID()) and reuse it only across retries of that same submit, passing it as idempotency_key; keep the server default but bind it to a submission-scoped value (e.g. ctx.request_id / a client nonce) rather than instruction text alone. If the text-based key is kept as a double-click guard, it must be time-bounded (e.g. append a short bucket) so it cannot dedupe forever. Independently, the UI must surface idempotent_replay === true instead of reporting a plain success.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration (real PG): apiCreateMission(db, ctx, { instruction: 'Fais le point sur les absences', source: 'cockpit' }) with NO idempotency_key → capture mission_id A. Run the SAME call again (simulating a legitimate re-submission later). Assert mission_id B !== A and idempotent_replay === false, and that pierre_rt_missions has 2 rows for the company. Today B === A and idempotent_replay === true. Also add a UI test asserting the composer surfaces a 'déjà confiée' state when idempotent_replay is true.

confirmed.title: B39 live email reports sent:true + audit send_allowed when the B37 provider silently dry-ran (EMAIL_DRY_RUN defaults to true and is ignored by the B39 config)
confirmed.currentBehavior: Two configs disagree and the adapter between them discards the caller's intent. `email-production/config.ts:63` computes `const dryRun = process.env.EMAIL_DRY_RUN !== "false"` and then NEVER USES IT — line 68 sets `dry_run: mode !== "live"` instead. So B39 ignores EMAIL_DRY_RUN. But `providers/resend.ts:48` still reads `const dry_run = getEnvBool("EMAIL_DRY_RUN", true)` — DEFAULT TRUE. `provider-adapter.ts:96` calls `resendChannelProvider.send({envelope, body, body_html})` and drops `input.mode` and `input.dry_run` entirely. Result: in B39 live mode (EMAIL_RUNTIME_MODE=live + EMAIL_SEND_LIVE=true per config.ts:15-20), the B37 provider short-circuits at l.187 because EMAIT_DRY_RUN is unset→true, returns ok:true with a synthetic `dry_run_...` id and never calls the Resend API. runtime.ts:360-384 then does `recordEmailSent(...)`, audits `send_allowed`, and returns `{ok:true, mode:"live", dry_run:false, sent:true}` — while types.ts:130 documents `sent` as "true only when live provider confirmed delivery". Nothing checks the `dry_run_` prefix on the message id. Reachable only via sendPierreEmailAction (pierre-email-actions.ts:89), which currently has no product caller — so this is a loaded gun for go-live rather than a live outage today.
confirmed.failureScenario: Operator follows the documented live contract (types.ts:12: "live: Requires EMAIL_SEND_LIVE=true + RESEND_API_KEY") and sets EMAIL_RUNTIME_MODE=live, EMAIL_SEND_LIVE=true, EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend, RESEND_API_KEY=re_... but does not set EMAIL_DRY_RUN=false (it is nowhere in the live checklist). Every email returns ok:true, sent:true, mode:"live", dry_run:false, provider_message_id:"dry_run_env_b39_...", audit event send_allowed, and the rate limiter is charged — while zero emails are transmitted. The audit log is a complete record of deliveries that never happened.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Make the caller's intent authoritative: have createResendEmailProviderAdapter pass input.mode/input.dry_run/input.sandbox_to into resendChannelProvider.send and have the provider honor them instead of re-reading env. Additionally, in live mode treat a provider result whose provider_message_id starts with `dry_run_` (or whose meta.dry_run===true) as a hard error, never sent:true. Remove the dead `dryRun` var in config.ts:63 or make B39 fail-closed when EMAIL_DRY_RUN!=="false" while mode==="live".
confirmed.regressionTest: With EMAIL_RUNTIME_MODE=live, EMAIL_SEND_LIVE=true, EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend, RESEND_API_KEY set, and EMAIL_DRY_RUN UNSET, call sendEmailProduction with the real default adapter and a stubbed `resend` module; assert either the Resend API is actually invoked, or the result has sent:false/ok:false — assert it can never be {sent:true, provider_message_id:/^dry_run_/}.

confirmed.title: Live-mode emails are silently redirected to RESEND_SANDBOX_TO while the result and audit record the real recipients as sent
confirmed.currentBehavior: `config.sandbox_to` here comes from `getResendConfig()` which reads `RESEND_SANDBOX_TO` from env (l.46) with NO awareness of the runtime mode. The B39 live branch in email-production/runtime.ts:322-329 explicitly passes `sandbox_to: null` to signal "no redirect", but provider-adapter.ts:96 discards that field and resendChannelProvider re-reads env. So if RESEND_SANDBOX_TO is still present in the live environment, every live email is delivered to that single address, while runtime.ts:376-390 returns `effective_recipients: decision.effective_recipients` (the REAL employee addresses), `sent: true`, `sandbox: false`, and the audit event (audit.ts via buildEmailAuditEvent) stores those real recipients.
confirmed.failureScenario: A staging→production promotion keeps RESEND_SANDBOX_TO=qa@clonestore.pro in the env while EMAIL_RUNTIME_MODE=live and EMAIL_DRY_RUN=false. Pierre sends 40 onboarding emails to 40 employees. All 40 land in the QA mailbox. The B39 result and the audit trail each report sent:true, sandbox:false, effective_recipients:[the real employee address]. Nobody can tell from the audit log that no employee was reached.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: buildResendPayload must take the redirect target from the caller (input.sandbox_to, which is null in live mode) rather than from env, and resendChannelProvider must refuse to apply a sandbox redirect when the caller declared mode==="live". If a redirect is applied, the returned result must set sandbox:true and effective_recipients to the redirected address so the audit trail is truthful.
confirmed.regressionTest: With mode=live and RESEND_SANDBOX_TO set, drive sendEmailProduction and assert either that the Resend payload `to` equals the real recipients, or that the returned EmailSendResult has sandbox:true and effective_recipients===[sandbox_to]. Assert {sent:true, sandbox:false, effective_recipients:[real]} is impossible while a redirect is in force.

confirmed.title: Role revocation is a permission no-op: the legacy `pierre_rt_members.role` column re-grants everything that was revoked
confirmed.currentBehavior: `DELETE /api/pierre/v1/members/[id]/roles/[role]` → `apiRemoveRole` (api.ts:163) → `Members.removeRole`, which deletes ONLY from `pierre_rt_membership_roles` / `pierre_rt_membership_custom_roles`. It never clears the legacy `pierre_rt_members.role` column. I grepped every write to that column across src/ and supabase/migrations/: it is written ONLY by ownership transfer (members.ts:310/315 and the SQL function at 2026-07-06__pierre_v28...:741/744). Meanwhile `resolveTenantContext` re-grants the revoked authority through TWO independent paths on the very next request: (a) line 122 unconditionally unions `ROLE_PERMISSIONS[member.role]` (the legacy code matrix) into the effective permission set regardless of which roles actually remain; and (b) line 97, when ALL system roles have been removed, `roleRows.rows.length` is 0 so `roleKeys` falls back to `[LEGACY_ROLE_TO_KEY[member.role]]`, which then drives the `pierre_rt_role_permissions` lookup and restores the FULL DB permission set for the very role that was just revoked. The audit log records `role_removed:<KEY>` and the route returns `{ok: true}`, so the operation looks successful.
confirmed.failureScenario: A member M was created from an invitation with roles ['ADMIN'], so `pierre_rt_members.role = 'admin'` and `pierre_rt_membership_roles = ['ADMIN']`. M leaves the HR team; an owner revokes the role: `DELETE /api/pierre/v1/members/M/roles/ADMIN` → 200 `{ok:true}`, audit `role_removed:ADMIN`. On M's very next request, `resolveTenantContext` runs: `roleRows` is now EMPTY → line 97 sets `roleKeys = ['ADMIN']` → `dbPerms` = every permission (the v3 seed grants OWNER/ADMIN all_perms, line 94-95) → PLUS line 122's `codeFallback = ROLE_PERMISSIONS['admin']` which includes `tenancy.admin`, `employee.write`, `mission.cancel`, `validation.decide`, `site.write`. M's effective permission set is byte-for-byte identical to before the revocation. M can still suspend/remove other members, invite new ones, decide validations, and write employee data. The same holds for a partial downgrade: giving M only VIEWER still leaves `codeFallback` grafting the full admin matrix on top, and `assertAssignableRoles` (members.ts:338) then reads `ctx.role === "admin"` → `isAdmin = true`, so M can re-grant themselves any role at will.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Make the legacy `role` column stop being a permission source. Two changes: (1) in `removeRole`/`assignRole`, keep `pierre_rt_members.role` in sync with the remaining `pierre_rt_membership_roles` (or set it to 'viewer' when no system role remains); and (2) in `resolveTenantContext`, stop unioning `codeFallback` unconditionally — apply the legacy code matrix ONLY when `roleRows.rows.length === 0 AND permRows.rows.length === 0` (i.e. a genuinely un-migrated account with no RBAC rows at all), never as an additive grant on top of a resolved DB role set. The line-97 fallback must likewise not fire when the membership has been deliberately stripped of roles.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test against the real runtime DB: create a company + member with legacy role 'admin' and membership_roles ['ADMIN']. Resolve the tenant context and snapshot `permissions`. Call `removeRole(db, ownerCtx, membershipId, 'ADMIN')`. Re-resolve the tenant context for the same user and assert `permissions` no longer contains `tenancy.admin`, `employee.write`, or `validation.decide`, and that `hasPermission(ctx, 'tenancy.admin') === false`. Add a downgrade case (assign VIEWER, remove ADMIN) asserting the resulting permission set is exactly VIEWER's.

confirmed.title: Client-supplied `field_values` override the tenant's real DB values in the contract generation context — a contract can be rendered, hashed, approved and signed with a forged employee/company identity
confirmed.quotedCode:
if (input.extra_values && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(input.extra_values, path)) values[path] = input.extra_values[path];
    else values[path] = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(canonical, path) ? canonical[path] : null;
confirmed.currentBehavior: POST /api/pierre/v1/contracts/{id}/generate takes `field_values` straight from the HTTP body (route.ts:11 → api.ts:224 → contracts.ts:206) and contracts.ts:152 splats it LAST into `extra_values`: `const extra = { "employment.start_date": dateStr(version.effective_from), "employment.end_date": dateStr(version.effective_to), ...fieldValues }`. contracts.ts:153 also adds every `Object.keys(fieldValues)` to `requested_fields`. buildStrictGenerationContext then validates only that the PATH is in the canonical registry (line 56) — it never checks the VALUE against the row it just loaded from the DB. The extra_values branch (line 113) wins over the `canonical` map built from pierre_rt_employees / pierre_rt_companies (lines 88-94). The module header claims 'every referenced entity is verified to belong to the active tenant … a cross-tenant or mismatched reference is refused (fail-closed)', but only entity IDs are verified, not the field values that are actually printed.
confirmed.failureScenario: An HR_OPERATOR (document.write + document.sensitive.write, the perms needed anyway) POSTs to /api/pierre/v1/contracts/{id}/generate with body {"field_values":{"employee.last_name":"MARTIN","company.legal_name":"ACME OFFSHORE LTD","employee.role_title":"Directeur","employment.start_date":"2019-01-01"}}. `employee.last_name` etc. are canonical paths so nothing is refused. buildContractRenderModel (contract-render-model.ts:51-52) builds employee_name/company_name from the forged values; the PDF, the DOCX, the document title (contracts.ts:263 `${policy.label} — ${model.employee_name}`) and the signature block all carry the forged identity, and canonicalContractHash is computed OVER the forged model. Readiness is `ready` (the forged values are non-empty, so `present()` passes at contract-readiness.ts:93). The contract is then approved, finalized and sent for signature to the REAL employee's e-mail (resolveSignatureRecipients reads emp.email from the DB), producing a signed employment contract whose parties/start date differ from the record of truth — and every downstream integrity check compares the forged hash to itself, so nothing detects it.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Allowlist what `extra_values` may carry. The declared intent in the type comment is 'a contract's effective dates / weekly hours … inject employment/date fields', so restrict caller-supplied paths to the `employment.*` namespace (as AMENDMENT_EFFECT_ALLOWLIST already does for amendments) and refuse any path the context itself loads from the DB (`company.*`, `employee.*`, `manager.*`, `site.*`, `dates.*`) with Errors.validation. Alternatively, keep extra_values but assert value === canonical[path] whenever `canonical` has the path.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test (src/lib/pierre/v1/__integration__/): create a governed contract for an employee whose last_name='DUPONT', then call generateContract(db, ctx, id, { field_values: { 'employee.last_name': 'FORGED', 'company.legal_name': 'FAKE SA' } }) and assert it REJECTS (Errors.validation) — and, if accepted for employment.* only, assert the rendered PDF text and the document title still contain 'DUPONT' and the real company legal name.

confirmed.title: CloneStore document renderer validates required variables AFTER injecting fallback placeholders — a contract full of "[Salaire]"/"[Entreprise]" is returned as ok:true with missing_variables:[]
confirmed.currentBehavior: resolveVariables() injects the template's literal fallbacks first (lines 162-166: `if (base[v.key] === undefined && v.fallback !== null) base[v.key] = v.fallback;`), and every required variable of the shipped contract template has a bracket placeholder as its fallback (template-registry.ts:65-70: company_name → "[Entreprise]", employee_name → "[Salarié]", salary → "[Salaire]", start_date → "[Date]"…). validateCloneDocumentVariables is then called with the RESOLVED map, and its presence test is `typeof val !== "string" || val.trim().length > 0` (line 83-86) — the string "[Salaire]" is a value, so the required variable is NEVER reported missing. Consequently `missingRequired === 0` and line 563 returns `ok: criticalIssues === 0 && missingRequired === 0` → true. The ONLY unresolved-placeholder scan is line 530: `const remainingPlaceholders = (content_text.match(/\{\{/g) ?? []).length;` gated by `if (remainingPlaceholders > 5)` — it is a WARNING, never a blocker, its threshold is arbitrary, and it is structurally blind to the `[X]` fallback family it just injected (it only matches `{{`).
confirmed.failureScenario: Call renderCloneDocument({ template: pierre_hr_contract_draft_v1, variables: {} }) (reachable from /api/pierre/use/document/preview, /api/pierre/use/document-templates/preview and /api/pierre/doc/generate). Result: ok=true, missing_variables contains only the 3 optional null-fallback vars, missingRequired=0, quality_score≈91, and content_text reads "Entre la société [Entreprise], … et [Salarié], demeurant [Adresse]" and "Le Salarié percevra une rémunération mensuelle brute de [Salaire]." plus three literal `{{trial_period}}`/`{{manager_name}}`/`{{collective_agreement}}` (3 ≤ 5, so not even the MANY_UNREPLACED_VARS warning fires). The caller/UI is told the document is complete and nothing is missing.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Validate required variables against the RAW input (input.variables + real profile sources), before fallback injection — e.g. `validateCloneDocumentVariables({ template, variables: mergeDocumentVariables(sourcesOnly, input.variables ?? {}) })` — and treat a fallback as a placeholder, not a value. Additionally, make the unresolved-placeholder scan a blocker with a regex covering every placeholder family the system can emit (`{{x}}`, `[X]`, `[À compléter…]`, `__X__`) and drop the >5 threshold.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit test in src/lib/clonestore/documents/__tests__/premium-documents.test.ts: `const r = renderCloneDocument({ template: getCloneDocumentTemplateById('pierre_hr_contract_draft_v1')!, variables: {} }); expect(r.ok).toBe(false); expect(r.missing_variables.filter(m => m.required).map(m => m.key)).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['company_name','employee_name','salary'])); expect(r.content_text).not.toMatch(/\[Salaire\]|\[Entreprise\]/);`

confirmed.title: A declared-but-empty template field is silently rendered as "—" in the FINAL contract and never blocks generation; the template's own `required` flag is dead
confirmed.quotedCode: if (val === null || val === undefined || val === "") { return "—"; }
confirmed.currentBehavior: `compileContractTemplate` is the ONLY engine used for real contract generation (contracts.ts:224). For a `{{path}}` that is declared in the template's `field_schema` AND present as a key in `context.values`, a null/empty value is substituted by an em-dash and NOTHING is recorded — `used_fields` only grows on success, and there is no `missing_fields` output at all. `generateContract` inspects only `compiled.unknown_fields` (contracts.ts:225). `evaluateContractReadiness` checks presence only for `policy.required_fields` (contract-readiness.ts:93), which is BASE_FIELDS = company.legal_name / first_name / last_name / role_title / start_date (+ weekly_hours or end_date). Every other contractual variable a template can carry (salary, classification, trial period, convention collective as a custom field, site address) is unchecked. `TemplateField.required` is declared on line 12 of the compiler and never read — while templates.ts:178 persists `required: !!f.required` and templates.ts:105 (mergeTemplate) DOES enforce it — but mergeTemplate is only used by `renderTemplatePreview` (templates.ts:353). So the preview says "incomplete" and the final generation says "ready".
confirmed.failureScenario: Published CDI template body contains "Rémunération brute mensuelle : {{compensation.base_salary}} EUR" with field_schema declaring compensation.base_salary {required:true}. Generation is called with field_values {"employment.weekly_hours":"35","compensation.base_salary":""} (blank form field). readiness.ready = true (base_salary is not in policy.required_fields), compiled.unknown_fields is empty, and the signed PDF reads "Rémunération brute mensuelle : — EUR". The contract passes approve → finalize → prepare_signature with no blocker anywhere.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Have `compileContractTemplate` return `missing_fields` (every placeholder that resolved to null/empty, plus every field_schema entry with `required:true` whose context value is empty) and make `generateContract` treat a non-empty `missing_fields` as a hard block exactly as it treats `unknown_fields`. Never emit a filler glyph in a final artifact — leave `{{path}}` intact like `mergeTemplate` does (templates.ts:97).
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: publish a contract template whose body references {{compensation.base_salary}} (declared required), then expect generateContract with field_values {"compensation.base_salary":""} to reject with a missing_required_fields blocker, and assert the rendered bytes never contain "—" for that clause.

confirmed.title: `company.legal_name` in a contract is read from the display-name column `pierre_rt_companies.name`; the real `legal_name` column is never read, so the required-field check can never fail
confirmed.quotedCode: "company.legal_name": company?.name ?? null, "company.display_name": company?.name ?? null, "company.slug": company?.slug ?? null,
confirmed.currentBehavior: The strict generation context (the one used for contracts) queries `select id, name, slug from pierre_rt_companies` (line 84) and maps BOTH `company.legal_name` and `company.display_name` to the `name` column. The schema has three distinct columns: `name text not null` (2026-06-15__pierre_v1_runtime.sql:27) plus nullable `legal_name` and `display_name` (2026-06-15__pierre_v3_enterprise_complete.sql:8-9) — and the other context builder, templates.ts:126, correctly selects `display_name, legal_name`. Consequence 1: the employer identity printed in the contract, in the signature block (`{ role: "L'employeur", name: company }`, contract-render-model.ts:68) and in the footer is the commercial/display name, never the registered legal name, even when `legal_name` is populated. Consequence 2: `company.legal_name` is in BASE_FIELDS (contract-policies.ts:40), but because it resolves to a NOT NULL column, `present(ctx.values["company.legal_name"])` is always true — the blocker `missing_required_fields` for the employer's legal name is structurally unreachable.
confirmed.failureScenario: Company row: name='Acme', legal_name=NULL (never filled during onboarding). Generate a CDI: readiness reports ready (legal_name 'present'), and the signed contract names the employer as "Acme" — a commercial label, not a legal entity. Same company with legal_name='ACME HOLDING FRANCE SAS' still prints "Acme", and a preview via renderTemplatePreview would show {{company.legal_name}} as missing — the two engines disagree on the same field.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Select `legal_name, display_name, name` and map `company.legal_name -> legal_name` (null when unset) and `company.display_name -> display_name ?? name`. With that mapping the existing BASE_FIELDS check will correctly block generation when the employer's legal name is not configured.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: company with name='Acme' and legal_name=NULL → generateContract must be rejected with blocker missing_required_fields including company.legal_name; company with legal_name='ACME HOLDING SAS' → the render model's company_name must equal 'ACME HOLDING SAS', not 'Acme'.

confirmed.title: Role revocation is a silent no-op: removeRole never clears the legacy `pierre_rt_members.role`, and resolveTenantContext UNIONS the legacy code matrix instead of using it as a fallback
confirmed.currentBehavior: `resolveTenantContext` derives permissions from BOTH the DB (`pierre_rt_membership_roles` -> `pierre_rt_role_permissions`) AND the hardcoded `ROLE_PERMISSIONS[member.role]` matrix keyed off the legacy `pierre_rt_members.role` column. Despite the comment calling it a "fallback", `codeFallback` is unconditionally UNIONed into the final permission set (line 124). Separately, `members.ts:371-381 removeRole()` deletes only from `pierre_rt_membership_roles` / `pierre_rt_membership_custom_roles` and NEVER updates `pierre_rt_members.role`. The only writers of that column are `transferOwnership` (members.ts:310, 315). No DB trigger syncs it (grepped all of supabase/migrations).
confirmed.failureScenario: Company has two owners, Alice and Bob (Bob promoted via transferOwnership, so `pierre_rt_members.role='owner'` AND membership_roles=[OWNER]). Alice demotes Bob: `DELETE /api/pierre/v1/members/{bob}/roles/OWNER` -> apiRemoveRole -> removeRole(). The last-owner guard passes (countActiveOwners=2), the OWNER row is deleted, the route returns `{ok:true}` and an audit row `role_removed:OWNER` is written. But Bob's `pierre_rt_members.role` is still 'owner'. On Bob's very next request, resolveTenantContext computes roleRows=[] -> roleKeys=[LEGACY_ROLE_TO_KEY['owner']]=['OWNER'] -> dbPerms = the full OWNER permission set; and codeFallback = ROLE_PERMISSIONS['owner'] re-adds tenancy.admin/queue.admin/employee.write regardless. Bob retains FULL owner privileges (tenancy.admin => can re-invite, re-assign roles, suspend Alice, list/patch roles). Even in the milder case where Bob keeps a second role (e.g. VIEWER), so roleRows is non-empty, the unconditional `codeFallback` union still re-grants tenancy.admin off the stale 'owner' column. Privilege revocation via the members API cannot actually revoke.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Two independent fixes, both needed. (1) `members.ts removeRole()` must also downgrade the legacy column in the same transaction -- recompute the highest remaining system role for that membership and `update pierre_rt_members set role = $x`, defaulting to 'viewer' when no system role remains (mirror this in assignRole for promotions). (2) `tenant-context.ts` must make `codeFallback` a TRUE fallback, not a union: only apply `ROLE_PERMISSIONS[member.role]` when `dbPerms.length === 0 && customPerms.length === 0` (i.e. an unmigrated membership with no role rows). Today a DB-side permission reduction can never take effect because the code matrix re-grants it.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test on the real PG harness: create a company with owner Alice; invite member Bob and `assignRole(bob,'OWNER')`; assert `resolveTenantContext(bob)` has 'tenancy.admin'. Then `removeRole(alice_ctx, bob_membership, 'OWNER')`. Re-run `resolveTenantContext(db,{user_id:bob,company_id})` and assert `hasPermission(ctx,'tenancy.admin') === false` and `ctx.role !== 'owner'`. Assert a follow-up `listMembers(bob_ctx)` throws Errors.forbidden. This currently fails: Bob is still a full owner.

confirmed.title: POST /api/pierre/v1/signatures/reconcile enforces entitlement but NO permission: a VIEWER can finalize signed contracts and dead-letter pending signatures
confirmed.currentBehavior: `reconcileSignatureRequests` is the ONLY state-mutating function in signatures.ts with no `requirePermission` call. Every sibling has one: `submitContractToSignatureProvider` (:104 `requirePermission(ctx, "document.approve")`), `cancelContractSignature` (:568 document.approve), `getContractSignature` (:585 document.read), `getSignatureEvidence` (:593 document.read). It is exposed at `src/app/api/pierre/v1/signatures/reconcile/route.ts:10` via `withProductAccess(req, "write_standard", (db, ctx) => Api.apiReconcileSignatures(db, ctx, { limit: b.limit }))`. `withProductAccess` is an ENTITLEMENT gate, not an RBAC gate: `resolveProductAccess(db, ctx)` (entitlements.ts:93) reads only `ctx.company_id` and is entirely role-blind, so any member of a company with an 'allowed' entitlement passes `write_standard`.
confirmed.failureScenario: A user holding only the VIEWER system role (permissions: mission.read, task.read, validation.read, employee.read, site.read -- no document.* at all) POSTs `{}` to /api/pierre/v1/signatures/reconcile. withProductAccess passes (company entitlement is 'allowed'; requirement 'write_standard' is permitted). reconcileSignatureRequests then, for every open signature request in the company: (a) calls the external e-signature provider `provider.getRequest(...)`; (b) if the provider reports done, calls `finalizeSignedContract` -- which downloads the signed document + evidence, writes `signed_document_version_id`, and transitions the employment contract to a SIGNED legal state -- an action that via the normal path requires `document.approve`; (c) if the provider reports declined/expired/cancelled/failed, calls `applyTerminalFromReconcile` -> `applyContractStatus`, driving the contract to a terminal workflow status. Worse, on any provider error `bumpRetry` increments retry_count, and after MAX_RECONCILE_RETRIES=5 sets `reconcile_status='dead_letter'`; the reconcile SELECT filters `reconcile_status <> 'dead_letter'`, so a viewer can call the endpoint 5 times and permanently exclude a legitimate pending signature from all future reconciliation. Tenant scoping is intact (every query is `where company_id=$1`), so this is not a cross-tenant leak -- it is an in-tenant privilege bypass. The existing test p83-b3-reconciliation.itest.ts only ever passes an `owner` context, so the gap is untested.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Add `requirePermission(ctx, "document.approve")` as the first statement of `reconcileSignatureRequests` (signatures.ts:531-532), matching submitContractToSignatureProvider/cancelContractSignature. It drives the same contract-signing state machine and must carry the same permission. If reconciliation is meant to be a background/worker sweep rather than an interactive user action, move it behind the `x-worker-token` gate used by /api/pierre/v1/worker/tick instead of exposing it on a member-authenticated route.
confirmed.regressionTest: In src/lib/pierre/v1/__integration__/p83-b3-reconciliation.itest.ts add: build a VIEWER TenantContext for the same company (membership with role_key VIEWER), submit a contract to signature as owner, then `await expect(S.reconcileSignatureRequests(h.db, viewer, {}, deps())).rejects.toMatchObject({ status: 403 })`. Also assert the viewer cannot burn retry_count: after the rejected call, `select retry_count, reconcile_status from pierre_rt_signature_requests` is unchanged. Owner path must still pass.

confirmed.title: Task approve/cancel/reschedule write the audit event WITHOUT the tenant key (and with columns no reader uses) — the human-approval record never appears in the audit trail or its export
confirmed.currentBehavior: The write uses the SERVICE ROLE (createAdminClient(), which bypasses RLS) and omits both tenant columns `user_id` and `agent_slug`. It also uses a column vocabulary (`level`/`event`/`payload`) that NO reader and NO other writer uses — the canonical shape is `user_id`/`agent_slug`/`event_type`/`message`/`meta_json` (see src/lib/pierre/tasks/execute-task.ts:153-161 and src/app/api/pierre/use/mission/[missionId]/continue/route.ts:338-349, which both stamp user_id + agent_slug). The insert result is never destructured, so any error is silently swallowed. The identical pattern exists in cancel/route.ts:219 (`event: "task_cancelled"`) and reschedule/route.ts:229 (`event: "task_rescheduled"`). Meanwhile the audit surface reads with the tenant predicate: src/app/api/pierre/use/audit-trail/route.ts:134-136 — `.from("pierre_task_logs").select("id, mission_id, task_id, event_type, message, meta_json, created_at").eq("user_id", userId).eq("agent_slug", "pierre")` — and the RLS policy is `pierre_task_logs_select_own ... using (auth.uid() = user_id)` (supabase/sql/pierre_rls_v1.sql:137-141).
confirmed.failureScenario: User A (owner of company A) POSTs /api/pierre/use/task/<taskId>/approve on a task awaiting_approval. loadOwnedTask correctly gates ownership, the task flips to `queued`, and the route returns {ok:true}. The audit row is then inserted with user_id = NULL (or the insert fails outright on the unknown `level`/`event`/`payload` columns — the error is never checked either way). User A then calls GET /api/pierre/use/audit-trail (or /audit-trail/export): fetchLogs filters `.eq("user_id", userId).eq("agent_slug","pierre")`, so the NULL-tenant row can never match, and neither can any row lacking agent_slug. The same happens in the employee-360 timeline (employee/[employeeId]/route.ts:328-335) and the task detail view (task/[taskId]/route.ts:232-235). Net effect: the human-in-the-loop approval — the single governance control point that lets a task run — and every cancellation and reschedule are ABSENT from the exported audit trail, which nonetheless presents itself as complete. Under RLS an authenticated client can never see the row either (auth.uid() = NULL is never true), so it is unrecoverable through the product.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Stamp the tenant key on every pierre_task_logs write and use the canonical column set. In approve/cancel/reschedule replace `level`/`event`/`payload` with `event_type`/`message`/`meta_json` and add `user_id: auth.userId, agent_slug: "pierre"` (auth.userId is already in scope from authenticateRequest). Check the insert error instead of discarding it. Ideally centralise on the existing helper shape used by src/lib/pierre/tasks/execute-task.ts:153-161 so no call site can omit the tenant key, and add a NOT NULL constraint on pierre_task_logs.user_id so a tenant-less audit write fails loudly rather than orphaning a row.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: as user A, create a task in `awaiting_approval`, POST /api/pierre/use/task/<id>/approve, then (a) assert a row exists in pierre_task_logs with user_id = A, agent_slug = 'pierre', event_type = 'task_approved', and (b) assert GET /api/pierre/use/audit-trail returns that event in its logs array. Both assertions fail today. Repeat for cancel and reschedule.

confirmed.title: /api/pierre/email/send writes an "email sent" audit fact + a fabricated provider ack, without ever calling any email provider
confirmed.currentBehavior: The POST handler validates the body, resolves a sender, then calls buildProviderMessageId() — a Date.now()+Math.random() string — and inserts a pierre_outbound_emails row with status:"sent" and provider_message_id set to that fabricated id. It then inserts a pierre_task_logs audit row with event "email_sent_direct" and message "Email envoyé : <subject>", and returns provider:{provider:"internal_stub", deliveryAccepted:true}. There is no fetch/provider call anywhere in the file: the module never imports sendPierreEmailWithProvider or any transport. The evidence records an external effect that never occurred, with a provider acknowledgement that was invented locally. This directly contradicts the runtime invariant proven elsewhere (src/lib/pierre/v1/executors.ts returns "awaiting_integration" for external effects, and src/lib/pierre/v1/communications.ts only writes 'submitted' with a REAL providerMessageId and reserves 'delivered' for a verified webhook). The row also omits user_id/agent_slug (the sibling writer src/lib/pierre/email/send.ts:28 sets user_id), so the falsified evidence has no actor attribution either, and it is written with the service-role client (createAdminClient), bypassing RLS.
confirmed.failureScenario: An authenticated user POSTs {to:"salarie@exemple.fr", subject:"Convocation à entretien préalable", body:"...", missionId:"<their mission>"} to /api/pierre/email/send. No email leaves the system. Yet pierre_outbound_emails now holds status='sent' with provider_message_id='pierre_1765...' and pierre_task_logs holds event='email_sent_direct' / "Email envoyé : Convocation à entretien préalable". The HR audit trail — the artifact used to prove a legally-required notification was delivered — asserts a delivery that never happened, with a provider reference that cannot be reconciled against any provider. The employee never receives the convocation; the record says they did.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Do not record a terminal 'sent' state without a real provider acknowledgement. Either (a) make the route honest — persist status 'awaiting_integration'/'draft' with provider_message_id null and log an event named for what actually happened (no "Email envoyé"), or (b) route it through the governed P8.4 pipeline (createCommunicationIntent → dispatch worker) which already records 'submitted' only after a real providerMessageId and 'delivered' only on a verified webhook. Also stamp user_id/agent_slug on the outbound row so the evidence carries an actor.
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test on the route handler: POST with a valid session and no provider configured, then assert (1) no pierre_outbound_emails row has status='sent', (2) any persisted provider_message_id is null (never a locally generated string), and (3) no pierre_task_logs row has event='email_sent_direct'. Add a guard test asserting the file contains no `status: "sent"` literal without a preceding provider call.

confirmed.title: Missing-info questions computed by Pierre are discarded: MissionView.missing_info is hardcoded [] while the mission is parked in awaiting_info with no way to answer
confirmed.quotedCode:
mission_id: mission.id, status: mission.status as MissionStatus, summary: mission.summary, risk: mission.risk,
    tasks: tasks.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, type: t.type, status: t.status, approval_required: t.approval_required, risk: t.risk })),
    missing_info: [],
confirmed.currentBehavior: createMission computes analysis.missing_info (analysis.ts detectMissingInfo → e.g. {id:"who", question:"Quel salarié / candidat / équipe est concerné ?", priority:"high"}) and uses it to park the task and the mission in awaiting_info (mission-service.ts:146 and :193), but persists only a COUNT in an event (`metadata: { count: analysis.missing_info.length }`, line 125) — the question text is never stored. assembleView (line 215) and apiGetMission (api.ts:50) then both return missing_info: []. awaiting_info tasks are never enqueued (only status === 'ready' is queued, line 182), and no V1 route accepts an answer: src/app/api/pierre/v1/missions/ exposes only [id], cancel, runtime, tasks, timeline, validations.
confirmed.failureScenario: Via CloneChat the user says « Relance. » (no subject). The model proposes create_mission, the user confirms, and /api/assistant/execute answers « C'est fait — Pierre a reçu votre mission. » The mission is then stuck in awaiting_info forever: the API reports missing_info: [] so no UI can display « Quel salarié est concerné ? », and there is no endpoint to supply it. The only exit is cancellation.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Persist analysis.missing_info (question text + priority) with the mission, return it in MissionView (assembleView and apiGetMission), surface it in the CloneChat execute response instead of the unconditional « C'est fait », and expose a route to answer it that re-runs planning (awaiting_info → planned is already a legal transition).
confirmed.regressionTest: Integration test: createMission({instruction:'Relance.'}) → mission.status === 'awaiting_info' AND view.missing_info contains the 'who' question; apiGetMission on that mission must return the same non-empty missing_info.

confirmed.title: createMission ignores the company's configured `default_autonomy_mode` and silently substitutes a hardcoded "normal"
confirmed.quotedCode:
// src/lib/pierre/v1/mission-service.ts:109
    const autonomy: AutonomyMode = input.autonomy_mode ?? "normal";
confirmed.currentBehavior: This is the honest-caller variant of finding #1 and needs no forgery. When any caller creates a mission WITHOUT passing `autonomy_mode` — which is what the cockpit and every `/api/pierre/v1/missions` client that omits the field does — the mode defaults to the string literal `"normal"`. `createMission` never queries `pierre_rt_companies.default_autonomy_mode`. I grepped every TS reference to that column: it is read only by `readCompanyAutonomyV1` (v1-loopback.ts:140), the CloneChat proposal builder, and `onboarding-completion-rules.ts:98`, which treats its presence as proof the tenant has set an "autonomy policy" (`missing_autonomy_policy`). The Pierre execution engine itself never consults it.
confirmed.failureScenario: During onboarding the owner deliberately selects the most cautious autonomy (`draft`), and onboarding-completion-rules.ts:98-99 records `evidence: { autonomy: 'draft' }` as satisfied. The owner then creates a mission from the Pierre cockpit, which POSTs to /api/pierre/v1/missions without an `autonomy_mode` field. `createMission` falls through to `"normal"`. Under `draft`, autonomy.ts:66 would have returned HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED for ANY external-side-effect task; under the substituted `normal`, autonomy.ts:69-70 returns AUTO_EXECUTE / EXECUTE_AND_NOTIFY for low-risk auto-executable actions. Tasks the owner explicitly configured to require review are auto-queued. The setting is presented as active in the product UI (/api/assistant/autonomy GET reads the column back and reports it as `current`), so the owner has no signal that the engine is ignoring it.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: In `createMission`, load `default_autonomy_mode` for `ctx.company_id` inside the transaction and use it as the mode (validated against `AUTONOMY_MODES`, falling back to "normal" only when the column is unset/invalid). The literal `"normal"` default must not shadow a configured company policy. This is the same one-line source-of-truth fix required by findings #1 and #3.
confirmed.regressionTest: Seed a company with `default_autonomy_mode='draft'`. Call `createMission` with NO `autonomy_mode` in the input. Assert the persisted mission row has `autonomy_mode='draft'` and that a task with `external_side_effect=true` is planned as `awaiting_validation`, not `ready`. Repeat for `high_autonomy` to assert the column is honored in both directions.

confirmed.title: createMission persists client-supplied `employee_id` / `site_id` with no tenant-existence and no site-scope check, unlike every other subsystem
confirmed.currentBehavior: `employee_id` and `site_id` arrive from the client body and are written straight to `pierre_rt_missions` with zero verification. `createMission` imports `requirePermission` from ./tenant-context but never imports or calls `canAccessSite` from ./rbac. Every other subsystem does: documents.ts:73 (`if (input.site_id && !canAccessSite(ctx, input.site_id)) throw Errors.forbidden("Site out of scope")`), employees.ts:127/142, generation-context.ts:60-62 (`Employee not found in this tenant` / `Employee out of site scope`), templates.ts:133, gdpr.ts:29, sites.ts:71. The DB offers no backstop either: 2026-06-15__pierre_v1_runtime.sql:51-52 declares `employee_id uuid,` and `site_id uuid,` as bare columns with NO foreign key and no composite (company_id, employee_id) constraint.
confirmed.failureScenario: A member scoped to site A (`pierre_rt_member_sites` restricts them, so `ctx.site_ids = ['A']`) POSTs to /api/pierre/v1/missions with `site_id: '<site B>'` and `employee_id: '<employee of site B>'`, or with an employee_id belonging to a different tenant entirely, or with a UUID for an employee that was archived/anonymized seconds earlier. All are accepted and persisted. `canAccessSite` — the site-scope gate the rest of the runtime enforces — is never consulted, so the mission is created out of the caller's site scope. The resulting row is a dangling reference: it points at an employee that does not exist under `ctx.company_id`. Downstream reads happen to be company-scoped (generation-context.ts:60 and runtime-action-handlers.ts:86 both filter `where company_id=$1 and id=$2`), so this does not currently leak another tenant's employee data — but it does mean mission records, audit trails, and the `employee_identified` readiness checks (controlled-mission-preflight.ts:98 asserts merely `Boolean(mission.employee_id)`) are satisfied by an unverifiable id, and a site-scoped member can plant missions outside their scope.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: In `createMission`, before `MissionRepo.insert`: if `input.employee_id` is set, verify the employee exists under `ctx.company_id` (`select 1 from pierre_rt_employees where company_id=$1 and id=$2`) and that `canAccessSite(ctx, emp.site_id)` holds, else throw `Errors.notFound`/`Errors.forbidden`; if `input.site_id` is set, verify it belongs to the tenant and that `canAccessSite(ctx, input.site_id)` holds — mirroring documents.ts:73 and generation-context.ts:60-72. Also add a composite FK `(company_id, employee_id) references pierre_rt_employees(company_id, id)` so the DB cannot hold a cross-tenant/dangling reference even if app code regresses.
confirmed.regressionTest: Two-tenant integration test: create company A and company B, each with an employee and a site. As an A-member, call `createMission` with company B's `employee_id` — assert it throws (404/403) and no mission row is inserted. Then, as an A-member restricted to site A1 via `pierre_rt_member_sites`, call `createMission` with `site_id = A2` — assert `Errors.forbidden('Site out of scope')`, matching the behavior already asserted for `createDocument`.

confirmed.title: verifyDocumentIntegrity can never return ok:true for a contract-generated version: it compares a canonical MODEL hash against the sha256 of the PDF bytes
confirmed.quotedCode:
const actual = f ? sha256(await storage.downloadBytes(f.object_key)) : null;
  const ok = !!v.content_hash && v.content_hash === actual;
confirmed.currentBehavior: generateContract stores the BUSINESS hash in the document version's content_hash: contracts.ts:267 `createVersion(tx, ctx, documentId, { rendered_pdf_file_id: pdfFileId, …, content_hash: canonical, … })` where `canonical = canonicalContractHash(model)` = sha256 of the canonicalized JSON model (contract-render-model.ts:103-110), which by design EXCLUDES the rendered bytes. finalizeVersion keeps that value (documents.ts:166 `let hash = v.content_hash;` — the PDF-derived fallback at line 167 only runs when content_hash is null). verifyDocumentIntegrity then downloads the real PDF and compares its sha256 to that model hash. The two hash different things, so `ok` is false for every legitimately generated contract document. The contract version DOES store the real `pdf_hash = sha256(pdf.bytes)` (contracts.ts:270) but the verifier never reads it.
confirmed.failureScenario: Generate a contract (any CDI/CDD), then call verifyDocumentIntegrity(db, ctx, documentId, 1). It returns { ok: false, content_hash: <canonical model hash>, file_sha: <real pdf sha> } and writes an 'integrity_verified {ok:false}' row into pierre_rt_document_access_log — on an untampered document. The verifier therefore returns ok:false whether or not the stored PDF was tampered with, so it can neither prove integrity nor detect tampering; any operator or audit relying on it gets a permanent false alarm and no signal.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Compare like with like: verify the rendered artifact against the stored artifact hash (pierre_rt_employee_contract_versions.pdf_hash, or a new pierre_rt_document_versions.artifact_sha256 written at createVersion from sha256(pdf.bytes)), and verify the business content separately against content_hash by recomputing canonicalContractHash. Return both results (artifact_ok, content_ok) instead of conflating them.
confirmed.regressionTest: Extend src/lib/pierre/v1/__integration__/p83-files-documents.itest.ts (or p83-b2g-contract-generation.itest.ts): after C.generateContract(...), assert `(await Docs.verifyDocumentIntegrity(h.db, owner, res.document_id, 1, deps())).ok === true`; then overwrite the stored object bytes in the fake storage and assert ok === false.

confirmed.title: A declared template field whose value is null is silently rendered as an em-dash "—" and reported in NO channel; only `unknown_fields` blocks generation
confirmed.currentBehavior: CompiledTemplate exposes `used_fields` and `unknown_fields` — there is NO `missing_fields` channel at all, and the compiler never reads TemplateField.required (declared on its own type at line 12 but never used). generateContract only blocks on the unknown set: contracts.ts:225 `if (compiled.unknown_fields.length > 0) { … throw Errors.validation(...) }`. The readiness engine only checks `policy.required_fields` and (for fixed-term) employment.end_date (contract-readiness.ts:93-101); a template-declared field that is not in the policy's required_fields list is never checked for presence. The parallel merge engine (templates.ts mergeTemplate) handles this correctly — it collects `missing` and sets `ready_for_final_generation: readyPreview && missing.size === 0` — but that engine is only used by renderTemplatePreview, not by contract generation.
confirmed.failureScenario: A CDD template (policy required_fields = base + employment.end_date) declares `employment.weekly_hours` and `employment.classification` in its field_schema and references them in a clause. The caller generates with field_values {"employment.weekly_hours": null, "employment.classification": ""} (both are canonical paths, so both land in `requested` and in context.values as null/""). compileContractTemplate substitutes "—" for both; contract-readiness only emits warn('weekly_hours_missing') (line 104) — a WARNING, never a blocker — and classification is not checked at all. readiness.ready === true, the PDF is generated with "Durée du travail : —" / "Classification : —", and the contract proceeds to approve → finalize → signature as a legally binding document with blanked-out contractual terms.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Add `missing_fields` to CompiledTemplate (populate it in the `val === null || val === ""` branch, and additionally for every field_schema entry with required:true that is absent/empty), and make generateContract fail closed on it exactly as it does for unknown_fields. Stop substituting a silent "—" for an absent declared value.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit test on compileContractTemplate: body "Durée : {{employment.weekly_hours}}", schema declaring it required, context.values = { 'employment.weekly_hours': null } → expect result.missing_fields to contain 'employment.weekly_hours' and expect generateContract with that field_values to reject with /missing/ rather than emit a PDF containing '—'.

confirmed.title: end-date-before-start-date is only checked for fixed-term policies; non-fixed-term contracts and amendments persist and render incoherent periods with no check anywhere
confirmed.currentBehavior: The coherence check (and the end-date format check) live INSIDE `if (policy.requires_end_date)`. CDI_FULL_TIME / CDI_PART_TIME / OTHER have `fixed_term:false, requires_end_date:false` (contract-policies.ts:62-63), so for them an end date is validated by nothing. Yet an end date is accepted and persisted for every contract type: `createGovernedContract` inserts `input.effective_to ?? null` with no comparison to `effective_from` (contracts.ts:99), same in `createContractVersion` (line 124) and `createContractAmendment` (line 489), and there is no CHECK constraint on the table. `resolveReadiness` then injects it as `"employment.end_date": dateStr(version.effective_to)`, and the caller can also force it via field_values. Nothing in the codebase ever compares the two dates outside the fixed-term branch.
confirmed.failureScenario: Create a CDI (or an amendment) with effective_from='2026-03-01' and effective_to='2025-01-01'. The row is stored as-is. Generate with field_values {"employment.weekly_hours":"35","employment.end_date":"2025-01-01"}: readiness runs no date-order check (requires_end_date=false), invalid_fields is empty, the contract is ready, and a template clause "{{employment.start_date}} au {{employment.end_date}}" renders a period that ends 14 months before it begins — then gets approved, finalized and signed.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Move the date-order and format checks out of the `requires_end_date` branch: whenever an end date is PRESENT (regardless of policy), assert DATE_RE and `end > start`. Additionally validate `effective_to > effective_from` at insert time in createGovernedContract / createContractVersion / createContractAmendment (and ideally add a DB CHECK), so an incoherent period is never persisted.
confirmed.regressionTest: Unit test on evaluateContractReadiness: CDI_FULL_TIME policy + context values start='2026-03-01', end='2025-01-01' → expect invalid_fields to contain 'employment.end_date_before_start' and blockers to contain 'invalid_fields'. Integration test: createGovernedContract with effective_to < effective_from must throw.

confirmed.title: The PDF renderer silently replaces every non-Latin-1 character with "?" in the final contract, corrupting employee/company names
confirmed.quotedCode:
// Drop anything still outside Latin-1 to avoid broken glyphs.
  return out.replace(/[^\x00-\xFF]/g, "?");
confirmed.currentBehavior: `toLatin1Safe` is applied to every string that reaches the PDF (title, subtitle with the employee + company names, clause paragraphs, table cells, signature block). Any character outside U+0000–U+00FF that is not in the small REPLACEMENTS list is turned into a literal "?". French accents survive; Polish/Czech/Turkish/Romanian/Vietnamese/Cyrillic characters do not. There is no warning, no missing/invalid field, and `validateOutput` only checks the %PDF header and %%EOF. The canonical business hash is computed from the model (contract-render-model.ts:103), NOT from the PDF bytes, so the corrupted PDF and the intact DOCX share the same canonical_hash and no drift check ever fires — the PDF is the artifact that is finalized, downloaded and sent to signature (`rendered_pdf_file_id` is the artifact checked in resolveReadiness, contracts.ts:167).
confirmed.failureScenario: Employee 'Łukasz Nowak' (or 'Nguyễn Van A'). generateContract renders the PDF subtitle/signature block as '?ukasz Nowak' / 'Nguy?n Van A'. The contract is clean, ready, approved, finalized, and prepared for signature with the employee's legal name misspelled in the binding artifact, while the DOCX of the same version spells it correctly and both carry the same canonical_hash.
confirmed.requiredCorrection: Either embed a font that covers the required repertoire, or make the loss detectable and fail-closed: have the PDF renderer report the set of characters it could not encode and have generateContract refuse to persist an artifact whose text was lossily transcoded (rather than emitting '?' into a legally binding document).
